ops.oldText: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below
ops.newText: grants to Licensee and, upon written notice to Licensor, its Affiliates a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below

ops.oldText: (c) sublicense, assign, lease, transfer or distribute any Licensed Technology, or operate and Licensed Technology for timesharing, rental, outsourcing, or service bureau operations, or to train persons (other than employees of the Licensee on the use of any Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use);
ops.newText: (c) sublicense, assign, lease, transfer or distribute any Licensed Technology (other than a transfer by Licensee to its successor in a merger or acquisition), or operate and Licensed Technology for timesharing, rental, outsourcing, or service bureau operations, or to train persons (other than employees of the Licensee on the use of any Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use);

ops.oldText: any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee for use in the Field of Use.
ops.newText: any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee and of its Affiliates for use in the Field of Use.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that the licence must reach our Affiliates and survive an M&A transaction; as drafted the grant runs to Licensee alone, use is confined to Licensee's employees, and clause (c) bars any transfer. We have taken the playbook fallback only: Affiliates are covered on written notice to Licensor (with the employee-only restriction conformed), and Licensee may transfer the licence to its successor in a merger or acquisition.
proposal.summary: Cover Licensee's Affiliates on written notice and let Licensee transfer the licence to its M&A successor

mappings.element: Licence transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
